title: Context Value Informed In-Context Reinforcement Learning
claim: Actor-only methods learn from high-variance Monte-Carlo returns; adding a critic that writes value tokens into context gives lower-variance, more stable adaptation.
layout: 2 panels, side-by-side, top-to-bottom flow, both converge on a central update box
description: The figure has two mirrored panels split by a dashed vertical line. The left panel, titled 'ICRL (Actor Only)', shows a context sequence of colored tokens (s, a, r) feeding a frozen Transformer that contains only a purple Actor block. Below it, a yellow 'Monte-Carlo credit signal' box holds the discounted-return formula, leading to a yellow 'High variance' label. The right panel, titled 'CV-ICRL (Actor-Critic)', has the same token sequence plus pink value tokens v. A green Critic block sits beside the Actor, and a dashed green arrow writes the predicted value back into the context. Below it, a green 'TD credit signal' box with the one-step TD formula leads to green 'Lower variance' and 'More stable test-time adaption' labels. A central 'Implicit in-context policy update' box receives arrows from both sides. Yellow versus green signals the contrast.
caption: From actor-only ICRL to context value informed (actor--critic-style) ICRL. (Left) The PG-like view models return-based credit assignment using the Monte-Carlo return $\widehat{G}_t=\sum_{k\ge0}\gamma^k r_{t+k}$. (Right) CV-ICRL augments the same Transformer with a context critic that predicts a context value $v_{t+1}$ and writes it back into the context, enabling a TD-style one-step target $\widehat{G}_t^{\mathrm{TD}}=r_t+\gamma v_{t+1}$ for lower-variance test-time adaptation.
abstract: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) has emerged as an effective paradigm for test time adaptation to unseen tasks without parameter updates. However, existing ICRL methods can exhibit brittle and unstable adaptions, and the mechanisms underlying such adaptions remain poorly understood. We provide a policy-gradient view of ICRL and argue that relying on trajectory-level return feedback can lead to high-variance updates when test time rollout is limited. Motivated by the actor--critic principle, we propose Context Value Informed ICRL (CV-ICRL), which equips the in-context policy with an explicit context value: the expected discounted return conditioned on the current state and accumulated interaction context. CV-ICRL trains a value head and writes its prediction back into the context as a value token, enabling TD-style return targets for lower-variance policy updates. Experiments on the Dark Room, Minigrid, and Procgen testbeds show that CV-ICRL substantially improves the stability of test time adaptation and achieves higher returns across tasks and environments. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Bluixe/CV-ICRL .
